extra.message: User-controlled 'username' from the POST body (sqli.get('username')) is interpolated directly into the SQL query string via f-string and passed to cur.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g., ' OR '1'='1) to bypass authentication or extract data. CWE-89 SQL Injection.

User-controlled 'mathexp' from the POST body (ssti.get('mathexp')) is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered at line 12. This is Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) which allows arbitrary Python code execution (e.g., {{7*7}} or RCE payloads). CWE-94 Code Injection.

extra.message: rfivuln() takes user-controlled 'imagelink' from the POST body (line 15) and passes it to fetchimage(), which performs requests.get(url=name) on the attacker-supplied URL and returns the response body. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery / Remote File Inclusion: attackers can make the server request internal services or remote content. CWE-918 SSRF.

requests.get() is called with verify=False, disabling TLS certificate validation. This makes the connection susceptible to man-in-the-middle attacks when fetching remote content. CWE-295 Improper Certificate Validation.

The attacker-controllable Host request header (read at line 12 via request.headers['Host']) is reflected unvalidated and unsanitized into the response body inside an HTML anchor tag. This is Host Header Injection which can be leveraged for cache poisoning, password reset poisoning, and reflected XSS. CWE-644 Improper Neutralization of HTTP Headers for Scripting Syntax.
